text:
maria: Heads-up — I enabled lightweight kernel-pick sampling (1%) on the g4dn canary pool for the next 2h to gather selection reasons. Will collect picks + short reason codes.
kevin: Nice. Do we have the format defined for the logs? Want to wire up a quick dashboard.
maria: Format is minimal to avoid perf noise. Example line:

```
[KPICK] model=resnet-transformer v=2.1 host=g4dn-07 seq_len=256 chosen=matmul_tiled reason=[arch=ampere,seq_bucket=128-512,cache=miss,batch=1] pick_id=abc123
```

maria: The reason array is ordered by priority (arch, seq_bucket, cache, batching) — each element is a short tag to avoid long strings.
sarah: Quick Q — does `cache=miss` mean KV cache absent or cold? How do we distinguish warm vs cold hits?
maria: Good call. We emit `cache=hit|warm|miss` where warm=recently populated but not full-match. Also `cache=stale` when we detect TTL mismatch.
devin: Any env flags to flip on more verbose traces for a single request during debugging?
kevin: I documented a couple. Use these in the runtime process env (temporary):

```
RDW_PICK_SAMPLING_RATE=0.01
RDW_PICK_LOG_LEVEL=info    # debug|info|trace
RDW_PICK_EXPLAIN=1         # emit structured reason tokens
RDW_PICK_FULLTRACE=0       # set to 1 for full KV + batch context (heavy)
```

maria: For reproducing a single trace from curl you can do: `curl -H "X-Debug-Pick:1" -d '{"input":...}' https://canary-infer/api/v1/generate` and the proxy will attach trace metadata to response headers.
kevin: Perfect. perf-bot just dropped a small flamegraph link for the canary window: <https://perf.internal/redwood/canary/1833456789>
perf-bot: summary: sampling=1% duration=2h requests=18.2k pick-logs=182 nodes with high matmul_tiled use on seq_len 256-384.

sarah: Early observation: on ampere machines we still see a non-negligible number of `fallback=generic_cuda` picks for long sequences > 1024. Might be a kernel compatibility gap.
maria: Yep. Those fallback picks include a reason code `compat=fallback` and a subreason `missing-optimized-kernel`.
devin: Can we autotune thresholds? E.g. when fallback rate > 2% for a seq_bucket, auto-add it to candidate compile queue?
maria: That's the plan for phase 2. Current telemetry supports computing per-(model,arch,seq_bucket) fallback ratios. We can trigger `autotune:enqueue` when `fallback_ratio > 0.02` and `requests>10k` for the bucket.
kevin: Any risk of chasing noise on tiny buckets? We should require min-traffic.
sarah: Agreed. Also prefer a rolling window and require that the candidate provides >5% median latency improvement in staging before promoting.
maria: Example of the pick telemetry doc we store (compact CSV-like line in s3):

```
pick_time,model,arch,seq_bucket,cache,chosen,pick_id,lat_ms,reason_flags
2026-11-04T09:13:22Z,resnet-transformer,ampere,256-512,miss,matmul_tiled,abc123,12.3,arch:ampere|seq:256-512|cache:miss|batch:1
```

kevin: Can we add a small numeric code for reason combos to save space? E.g. reason_code=0x1A3
maria: We're outputting both short tag string + hashed code so queries can use either. Hash stable across releases.
devin: Small perf note — enabling `RDW_PICK_FULLTRACE=1` on busy nodes added ~0.6% p99 token latency in my local test. Keep default off.
infra-bot: deploy: pick-sampling 1% enabled on g4dn-canary (maria) — rollout id: rs-2026-11-04-09:14
sarah: Next steps: collect 24h of samples, generate per-arch heatmaps, and propose autotune enqueue rules. I'll mock a dashboard with the reason breakdown.
kevin: I'll add a lightweight alert if fallback_ratio for any seq_bucket > 1.5% over 6h.
maria: Thanks all. I'll post the aggregated CSV to the shared bucket when 2h is done. :rocket:
